title: Adaptive Probe-and-Pivot Scheduler for multi-GPU prefill/decode and attention kernel selection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a runtime scheduler that continuously probes short-lived latency/throughput signals and pivots kernel selection and inter-device routing during prefill and decode to improve 99th-percentile latency while preserving throughput. The scheduler coordinates tensor- and pipeline-parallel stages, opportunistically overlaps NCCL transfers, and manages microbatch slicing so attention kernel choices and KV cache alignment are adaptive to real-time congestion and model shape variability.
acceptance_criteria: Reduces 99th-percentile latency on full-stack load tests by >= 18% for mixed request sizes compared to baseline runtime-1.20 with static kernel selections
No regression in median throughput beyond 5% at production-like concurrency for Llama-3-13B baseline and a 32k-context model variant
Can detect and mitigate a degraded device/peer (simulated 30% bandwidth drop) by pivoting to alternate kernel variants and routing within 200ms with controlled hedging
Exposes observability: per-request kernel decisions, NCCL overlap windows, and probe signal histograms in Console traces and runtime metrics
implementation_steps: Design probe protocol: lightweight latency microbenchmarks per device pairing and per-kernel path (prefill kernel vs fused attention) executed at configurable intervals
Implement Probe Manager: aggregated rolling stats, anomaly detection, and confidence scoring for pivot decisions
Scheduler integration: decision hooks that pick kernel variant and microbatch split per request for prefill vs decode path
NCCL overlap controller: schedule explicit overlap windows and hedging tokens based on probe signals and topology
KV cache alignment heuristics: ensure pivot keeps cache offsets compatible or performs fast cache rekeying on canary flows
End-to-end tests: synthetic and trace-driven workloads; build harness to replay production traces with fault injection
Observability: add kernel-decision spans, probe metrics, and sampling for long-tail latency traces to Console
Canary rollout: staged enablement with per-route flags and automatic rollback on SLO regressions
decisions: Use short-running probe tasks (<=5ms) to avoid impacting steady-state throughput; probes will be rate-limited per GPU and biased toward low-utilization windows
Pivot granularity will be at request level for latency-sensitive routes and at batch window level for high-throughput routes
Default hedging policy: single speculative reroute to adjacent device-group with exponentially decaying frequency under repeated failures
Kernel selection will prefer fused attention variants when probe confidence indicates bandwidth is stable; fallback to non-fused kernels under high interconnect jitter
tradeoffs: Probing frequency vs perturbation: more probes give faster adaptation but increase noise and overhead. We keep probes low-frequency and correlated with request sampling.
Latency vs throughput: aggressive hedging lowers tail latency but increases token work. We'll gate hedging by customer tier and route SLA.
Complexity vs observability: adding pivoting logic increases state and debugging surface; instrumentation must be complete to make this safe in production.
benchmarks_targets: Target environment: 8xA100 40GB in tensor+pipeline layout matching production-topology
Test workloads: small-chat (prefill 16 tokens + decode 128), long-context (prefill 16k + decode 512), and embedding-like small-prefill-only flows
Latency SLOs: median <= 60ms for small-chat, p99 <= 450ms after pivot optimizations
Throughput constraint: <=5% median throughput regression allowed on sustained QPS when feature enabled
testing_plan: Unit tests for Probe Manager logic with synthetic latency distributions
Integration tests across simulated heterogeneous bandwidth scenarios (random 10%-70% peer bandwidth degradation)
Replay tests using sampled production traces (anonymized) to validate pivot decisions and cache handling
Fault-injection: kill one device, throttle links, and measure failover time and error surface
A/B test in staging with 10% traffic and compare p50/p95/p99 and token costs
rollout_plan: Internal dogfood: enable for non-critical routes in staging cluster; gather metrics for 48h
Canary: enable for 5% of production traffic routed to t3-dedicated pools for 1 week, with automated revert on SLO breach
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% per route with validation gates
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window with alerting on increased token cost or errors
observability_metrics: slo_error_rate and realtime_p99_latency for routes with feature enabled
blockers: Need revised NCCL tuning knobs surfaced via infra config (infra ticket INF-204) — infra owner assigned
